title: Enabling Efficient Mobile Tracing with BTrace
problem: Existing mobile tracing tools use distributed per-core or per-thread buffers that prioritize performance but have a high probability of missing crucial trace events in smartphone scenarios, where event ordering and completeness are critical for diagnosing stability issues.
motivation: Smartphones require detailed, complete system traces for diagnosing stability problems and optimizing user experience, but the distributed buffer designs of server-oriented tracers are poorly suited to mobile's constrained and event-dense environments.
method: BTrace introduces a mobile-optimized tracing design that addresses the incompleteness problem of per-core/per-thread distributed buffers by redesigning the buffer management and synchronization strategy for smartphone workloads. The system uses a centralized or coordinated buffering approach that preserves event completeness while maintaining acceptable performance overhead, tailored to the smartphone system software stack.
key_novelty: A tracing buffer architecture designed specifically for smartphones that trades some throughput for substantially improved trace completeness, avoiding the event loss endemic to per-core distributed tracing on mobile.
contributions: Characterization of why distributed per-core/per-thread tracing buffers lead to high event loss on smartphones
Design of BTrace, a mobile-specific tracing system with improved event completeness
Demonstration that complete tracing is achievable on smartphones without prohibitive performance overhead

metrics.other: improved trace completeness (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: per-core and per-thread distributed tracing tools (e.g., Linux ftrace, Android tracing)
limitations: Specific completeness and overhead numbers, and comparison against state-of-the-art mobile tracers, are not available from the abstract.
primary_theme: Complete event tracing for smartphone systems
